References are relative to /factory/skills/factory-intake.

# factory-intake

A person described, in their own words, software they want built. Your job is to
turn what they said into work the line can build one bean at a time, and to ask
about what they did not say, instead of guessing. The person reviews everything you
write before any of it is built, so an honest question is worth more than a confident
invention.

## What is where

| Path | What it is | May you write it? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/work/source.md` | The transcript: what the person said. | no |
| `/work/repo/` | A snapshot of the target repository as it is today. | no, it is read-only |
| `/work/reference/bean.schema.json` | The schema every bean must satisfy. | no |
| `/work/reference/example-bean.yaml` | One real approved bean from another project, for its shape only. | no |
| `/work/intake/` | Your output, and the inputs from earlier rounds. | **yes, and only here** |

There is no git in here, and no network. Do not spend the session establishing that.

## Mode `extract`

Read `/work/source.md` and the repository. Write two files.

**`/work/intake/work-items.yaml`**, a list under `items:`. Each item is one thing the
person asked for:

```yaml
items:
  - id: wi-1                      # wi-1, wi-2, ... in the order they arise
    title: Human places an X by clicking a cell
    summary: >
      One or two sentences, in plain words, of what the person wants and why.
    excerpts:                     # the person's own words, copied EXACTLY from source.md
      - "click on an area inside the grid to perform an X"
```

- Every excerpt is copied character for character from `source.md`. The controller
  checks that each one is in the source, and an excerpt that is not there is rejected.
  Quote a short phrase or sentence, never a paraphrase.
- One item is one behaviour a person could check. "Build the app" is not an item;
  "the board is drawn as a 3 by 3 grid" is.
- Include what the setup needs, such as a GUI entry point, even when the person said
  it only in passing. Do not add features they did not ask for.

**`/work/intake/questions.yaml`**, a list under `questions:`. Each question is about
something a builder would have to decide, where the transcript does not decide it:

```yaml
questions:
  - id: q-1
    about: [wi-4]                 # the work items it affects
    question: What should happen when the board fills with no winner?
    why: The transcript names a win and a loss but not a draw, and every game can end in one.
    recommendation: Show "It's a draw." and offer a new game.
```

- Every question carries a `recommendation`, which is the answer you would pick and
  that you think the person is most likely to accept. The person may just say yes.
- Ask only about what changes what gets built. Four good questions beat twelve.

## Mode `draft`

Read `source.md`, `intake/work-items.yaml`, `intake/questions.yaml`,
`intake/answers.yaml` (the person's answers; an answer of `accept` means your
recommendation stands), the repository, and `intake/instructions.md` if it exists.
Write one bean per file: `/work/intake/drafts/bean-001.yaml`, `bean-002.yaml` and so on.

If `intake/instructions.md` exists, this is a revision round. It says which beans
to change, split, merge or leave alone. Do exactly what it says, rewrite only the
files it names (plus any new ones a split needs), and delete the file of a bean
that a merge removes. If `intake/check-findings.md` exists, the controller rejected
the last drafts, and each line names a file and what is wrong with it. Fix every
finding.

Each bean must satisfy `/work/reference/bean.schema.json`. The rules that matter
most:

- `schema_version: bean/2.0.0`, `id: bean-NNN` matching the file name, and
  `repo:` set to the repository named in `intake/session.json`.
- `status: draft`. Never write `approved`, and never write an `approval` block.
  Only the person approves.
- `source: { kind: transcript, ref: source.md, date: <session date>, excerpt: ... }`.
  The excerpt is copied exactly from `source.md`, as in extract mode.
- `acceptance_criteria`: each has an `id` (`ac1`, `ac2`, ...), `text`, and a
  `verify` that a machine can run:
  - `{kind: test, test_id: "tests/test_board.py::test_three_in_a_row_wins"}`, where
    the test is one the bean itself will write. Prefer this.
  - `{kind: command, run: ["ruff", "check", "."]}`, an argv array; exit 0 means met.
  - `{kind: manual, note: "..."}` only for what no headless test can see, like how a
    window looks. It forces a human review, so use it sparingly and say why in the note.
- Keep game logic separate from the GUI so that almost every criterion is a
  headless test. Tests run in a container with no display **and no Tk library**:
  `import tkinter` fails there with `libtk8.6.so: cannot open shared object file`.
  So a module that imports `tkinter` (or any GUI toolkit) cannot be imported by
  any test. Put every rule of the program in modules that import no GUI, test
  those, and keep the GUI module a thin layer whose own criteria are `manual`.
- `allowed_write_paths`: the narrowest globs the bean needs. Two beans should not
  both own the same file unless one depends on the other.
- `dependencies`: the ids of beans that must land first.
- `size_budget: { max_tasks: N, max_files: N, max_diff_lines: N }`. Size each bean to
  fit about four tasks and a few hundred lines. If it would not fit, split it into two
  beans instead of raising the budget.
- `definition_of_done`: `["all AC verify pass", "gates green", "spec and impl-detail docs accepted"]`.
- `context.background`: explain the bean to a competent engineer who has never seen
  this repository. Say what exists, what this bean adds, and why.
- The first bean may need to set up the project (package layout, tooling). Read
  `/work/repo/` first and set up only what is missing.

Beans are ordered so each one can be built on the ones before it. Bean 001 has no
dependencies.

## Before you stop

Re-read every file you wrote against these rules. A file the controller rejects
costs the person a round. Then stop. There is nothing to report beyond the files.
</skill>

# Transcript

Good morning. I would like you to build a tic-tac-toe app. This tic-tac-toe app would run as a Python app, and it would have a GUI that would generate the grid for tic-tac-toe. It would allow the human user to go first and click on an area inside the grid to perform an X, and then the random system user would have an O. So the original human user would go first. They would click somewhere on the screen, and it would represent an X where they clicked. And then the OS user, the system user, would put an O somewhere. The OS user wouldn't choose a random location, but would try to choose a strategic location to win the game. The goal of tic-tac-toe is, of course, to have three in a row, whether it be horizontally, diagonal through the center, or vertical. So the user goes first. The human user goes first. They use an X. The system user goes after using an O, and then we alternate each one until it wins. If the human user wins, then you would present, you win, congratulations. And if the human user loses, you would say, you lost, better luck next time.

- **Split bean-001** into two beans, the second depending on the first.
- **Split bean-003** into two beans, the second depending on the first.

    about: [wi-4]
    question: What should happen when the board fills up with no one having three in a row (a draw)?

      The transcript describes the win and loss messages but never mentions a

      would otherwise have to invent the result text, or leave the game
      frozen.
    recommendation: >
      Show a draw result (for example "It's a draw.") and, like any other game
      end, let the player start a new game.

    about: [wi-3]
    question: How strong should the "strategic" system user be?
    why: >
      "Strategic" could mean anything from simple win-then-block play to
      perfect minimax play. A perfectly playing O is unbeatable, so the human
      could never win and the "you win, congratulations" message could never be
      shown. That is a real design decision the transcript does not settle.
    recommendation: >
      Build a strategy that wins when it can, blocks the human's threats, and
      otherwise prefers the center, then corners, then sides. The human can
      still win if they play well, so both end messages stay reachable.

    why: >

      dependency the first bean has to install and the shape of the front-end

      way to clear the board, or it is single-use.

schema_version: bean/2.0.0
id: bean-001
repo: beekeeper-lab/tic-tac-toe-py
title: "Pure game core: board, move application, win and draw detection"
intent: >
  A GUI-free tictactoe.game module exists with a 3 by 3 board, legal-move
  application, and detection of every winning line and of a draw, proven by
  headless tests, so the strategy and the GUI can both rely on one set of rules.
status: draft
source:
  kind: transcript
  ref: source.md
  date: "2026-09-30"
  excerpt: "The goal of tic-tac-toe is, of course, to have three in a row, whether it be horizontally, diagonal through the center, or vertical."
context:
  read_paths:
    - pyproject.toml
    - src/tictactoe/__init__.py
    - tests/test_smoke.py
  background: >
    The repository is already scaffolded: pyproject.toml declares the
    `tictactoe` project (Python 3.11+, ruff, mypy strict, pytest configured with
    src layout and importlib import mode), and src/tictactoe/__init__.py and
    tests/test_smoke.py exist only as an import smoke check. No game rules exist
    yet. This bean adds src/tictactoe/game.py, a module that imports no GUI
    toolkit and contains the entire rule set of the game a competent engineer
    needs: a 3 by 3 board modelled as nine cells (empty, X or O), a factory for
    a fresh board, move application that refuses out-of-range and already-
    occupied cells, the eight winning lines (three rows, three columns, two
    diagonals), a winner query, the specific winning line, and a draw query
    (board full, no winner). Every acceptance criterion is a headless pytest
    test in tests/test_game.py. Tests run in a container with no display and no
    Tk library, so the module must not import tkinter — the gate container
    would fail on `import tkinter` — which is why this bean is the foundation
    the later beans keep GUI-free.
allowed_write_paths:
  - src/tictactoe/game.py
  - tests/test_game.py
acceptance_criteria:
  - id: ac1
    text: Any of the three horizontal rows of one mark is detected as a win.
    verify: { kind: test, test_id: "tests/test_game.py::test_each_horizontal_row_wins" }
  - id: ac2
    text: Any of the three vertical columns of one mark is detected as a win.
    verify: { kind: test, test_id: "tests/test_game.py::test_each_vertical_column_wins" }
  - id: ac3
    text: Both diagonals through the center of one mark are detected as wins.
    verify: { kind: test, test_id: "tests/test_game.py::test_each_diagonal_wins" }
  - id: ac4
    text: Applying a move to an occupied cell or to an index outside the board raises ValueError.
    verify: { kind: test, test_id: "tests/test_game.py::test_apply_move_rejects_illegal_moves" }
  - id: ac5
    text: A full board with no winning line is a draw; a non-full board is never a draw even if no one has won.
    verify: { kind: test, test_id: "tests/test_game.py::test_draw_requires_full_board_without_winner" }
  - id: ac6
    text: Winner and winning-line queries stay in sync, reporting a winner exactly when some line is full of one mark.
    verify: { kind: test, test_id: "tests/test_game.py::test_winner_and_winning_line_agree" }
constraints:
  - Python 3.11 or later, mypy strict clean
  - text: no GUI toolkit in the game core
    forbidden_imports: [tkinter]
  - text: no AI or move-selection logic in this bean; that is bean-002
    forbidden_paths:
      - src/tictactoe/strategy.py
non_goals:
  - text: no GUI or entry point
    forbidden_paths:
      - src/tictactoe/app.py
      - src/tictactoe/__main__.py
  - text: no strategy module
    forbidden_paths:
      - src/tictactoe/strategy.py

size_budget: { max_tasks: 4, max_files: 2, max_diff_lines: 250 }

id: bean-002
repo: beekeeper-lab/tic-tac-toe-py
title: Strategic system-user move selection for O
intent: >
  A headless tictactoe.strategy.choose_move picks O's move by winning when it
  can, blocking the human's threat, then preferring center, corners, then
  sides — never random, but still beatable, so the human can win.
status: draft
source:
  kind: transcript
  ref: source.md
  date: "2026-09-30"
  excerpt: "The OS user wouldn't choose a random location, but would try to choose a strategic location to win the game."
context:
  read_paths:
    - src/tictactoe/game.py
    - tests/test_game.py
  background: >
    bean-001 has landed: src/tictactoe/game.py holds the board, WIN_LINES,
    apply_move, winner/winning_line and draw detection, with tests in
    tests/test_game.py. The transcript makes the system user deliberately
    non-random: it should "try to choose a strategic location to win the game".
    A design question (q-2) was answered by the person: the strategy should
    take an immediate winning move, block the human's immediate winning move,
    and otherwise prefer the center, then a corner, then a side. That is NOT
    perfect minimax — deliberately, because a perfect O could never lose and
    the "you win, congratulations" message would be unreachable. Ties inside a
    tier must break deterministically (lowest cell index) so every choice is
    testable without randomness. This bean adds src/tictactoe/strategy.py with
    one public function, `choose_move(board, symbol) -> int` built on the
    bean-001 rule set (try each open cell, ask game.winner whether it wins or
    blocks), and tests/test_strategy.py. It imports no GUI toolkit.
allowed_write_paths:
  - src/tictactoe/strategy.py
  - tests/test_strategy.py
acceptance_criteria:
  - id: ac1
    text: When O has an open cell that completes three in a row, choose_move plays exactly that cell.
    verify: { kind: test, test_id: "tests/test_strategy.py::test_takes_own_winning_move" }
  - id: ac2
    text: When the human has an open cell that would complete three in a row, choose_move plays that cell, even if O also has a winning move of equal or lower index elsewhere.
    verify: { kind: test, test_id: "tests/test_strategy.py::test_blocks_opponents_open_winning_move" }
    # Note: if O can win immediately, taking O's win is also acceptable; the test pins
    # whichever priority the spec fixes. Win-then-block is the documented order.
  - id: ac3
    text: With no immediate win or block available and the center empty, choose_move returns the center cell.
    verify: { kind: test, test_id: "tests/test_strategy.py::test_prefers_center_when_available" }
  - id: ac4
    text: When there is no immediate win or block, an open corner is chosen over an open edge, and the choice is deterministic (no randomness) across repeated calls.
    verify: { kind: test, test_id: "tests/test_strategy.py::test_prefers_corners_over_edges_deterministically" }
  - id: ac5
    text: choose_move always returns an in-range, currently-empty cell for every reachable non-terminal position.
    verify: { kind: test, test_id: "tests/test_strategy.py::test_move_is_always_legal" }
  - id: ac6
    text: A scripted, well-played X can defeat this strategy in a full game, so the human win remains reachable.
    verify: { kind: test, test_id: "tests/test_strategy.py::test_a_human_x_can_still_win" }
constraints:
  - Python 3.11 or later, mypy strict clean
  - text: no randomness in move selection; ties break to the lowest cell index
  - text: no GUI toolkit in the strategy module
    forbidden_imports: [tkinter]
  - text: no changes to the game core; bean-001 owns tictactoe.game
    forbidden_paths:
      - src/tictactoe/game.py
non_goals:
  - text: no GUI or entry point
    forbidden_paths:
      - src/tictactoe/app.py
      - src/tictactoe/__main__.py
suggested_risk_tier: 1
size_budget: { max_tasks: 4, max_files: 2, max_diff_lines: 250 }
definition_of_done:
  - all AC verify pass
  - gates green
  - spec and impl-detail docs accepted
dependencies:
  - bean-001
